title: The Secret War and the Silent Answer: Casey from Grosvenor Street to Glen Cove
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Elmhurst, Queens, the birth the record barely fixes
stops.date_confidence: date attested (Wikipedia, 'William J. Casey'); the place is reconstruction, since that article says only 'New York City' and Elmhurst comes from Persico's biography, not consulted directly
stops.campa: William Joseph Casey is born in New York City on the thirteenth of March, nineteen thirteen. The reachable record fixes the day and says only that much about the ground: the city. Elmhurst in Queens comes from Joseph Persico's biography, a book this pass could not open, and the pin therefore stands on a biographer's word rather than on a certificate. The family does not stay long in the borough. They go east onto Long Island, and the child born in a city grows up in a county. The record about Casey is thinner than the story about him, and it begins being thinner here.
suggested_refs: Joseph E. Persico, Casey: The Lives and Secrets of William J. Casey (1991), the source of the Elmhurst detail

stops.name: Bellmore, the Irish Catholic house on the south shore
stops.date_confidence: traditional; Wikipedia attests the upbringing at Bellmore but fixes no year, and 1920 is a placeholder inside his childhood
stops.campa: He is raised in Bellmore, on the south shore of Nassau County, in an Irish Catholic household loyal to Democratic machine politics. The loyalty does not descend. The son will spend his working life inside the Republican Party, running first its money and at last its intelligence service. Nobody in the family records the moment the switch is made. Long Island holds him from here to the end. Bellmore, then Roslyn Harbor, then a hospital at Glen Cove: three towns within twenty miles of each other bracket a life spent mostly elsewhere.
suggested_refs: The Bellmore of the 1920s, a south-shore village of the Long Island Rail Road

stops.name: Fordham University, Rose Hill, the bachelor's degree
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Wikipedia); month inferred from the ordinary commencement calendar and defaulted
stops.campa: Casey takes his bachelor's degree from Fordham, the Jesuit university at Rose Hill in the Bronx, in nineteen thirty-four. The training is in argument and in Catholic doctrine. The prose he writes for the rest of his life is a lawyer's prose built on distinctions, and his loyalty to Church institutions outlasts every government he serves. Half a century later he will fly to Rome to brief a pope, or so one journalist reports, and the Jesuits are the reason anyone finds that report plausible.
suggested_refs: Fordham University, Rose Hill campus, class of 1934

stops.name: Catholic University of America, the year that is not documented
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; no primary enrolment record was located, and neither dates nor coursework are established. The 1935 date is a placeholder between Fordham and St. John's
stops.campa: Between the Bronx and the law he is said to pursue graduate study at the Catholic University of America in Washington. The episode is thinly documented. No enrolment record was located in this pass, no coursework is named, and no year is fixed by any source reachable here, so the stop is entered as a gap with coordinates rather than as an event. It is entered anyway, because Washington appears here for the first time, and he will hold five federal offices in that city before he is done.
suggested_refs: Catholic University of America registrar records, mid-1930s, not retrieved
sources: Wikipedia, 'William J. Casey'; gap: no primary enrolment record located

stops.name: St. John's University School of Law, Brooklyn, the LL.B.
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Wikipedia); month inferred from the ordinary commencement calendar and defaulted
stops.campa: In nineteen thirty-seven Casey earns his LL.B. from St. John's University School of Law, then housed in Brooklyn. The degree carries him into Wall Street practice within a year and, thirty-four years after that, into the chairmanship of the Securities and Exchange Commission, which is the same body of law seen from the other side of the table. He is a tax lawyer before he is anything else. The publishing house he will run and the insurgencies he will finance rest on the same working knowledge: where money is permitted to go and where it is not.
suggested_refs: St. John's University School of Law at its Brooklyn premises, 1937

stops.name: Lower Manhattan, partner at Buckner, Casey, Doran and Siegel
stops.date_confidence: attested to the span 1938-1942 (Wikipedia); month and day defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Casey becomes a partner in the Manhattan firm of Buckner, Casey, Doran and Siegel and builds a tax practice in the years when federal regulation is multiplying faster than business can read it. The partnership runs to nineteen forty-two, when the war takes him. Note what is not here: the gathering pass credited him with founding the Research Institute of America alongside Leo Cherne, and he did not. RIA grew from Carl Hovgard and Cherne's own venture of the mid-thirties. Casey joins a going concern rather than starting one, which is a habit.
suggested_refs: Buckner, Casey, Doran and Siegel, Lower Manhattan tax practice, 1938-1942

stops.name: Midtown Manhattan, chairman of the Research Institute board of editors
stops.date_confidence: span 1938-1949 attested (Wikipedia); month defaulted. The Midtown coordinate is a generic point, not a located address, and is carried only for want of one
stops.campa: For eleven years Casey chairs the board of editors of the Research Institute of America, a publisher whose business is translating tax and regulatory law into instructions a company can follow. The work makes him wealthy before the war ends. It also gives him the shape of mind that his colleagues will recognize in him at Langley forty years on: a man who reads enormous quantities of paper fast and wants the operative sentence rather than the argument around it. He will trust a summary he has written himself over a briefing anyone else prepares.
suggested_refs: Research Institute of America editorial offices, New York, 1938-1949

stops.name: 2430 E Street NW, Washington, joining the Office of Strategic Services
stops.date_confidence: Naval Reserve service 1943-1946 attested (Wikipedia); the month of his entry into OSS is not fixed in the reachable sources and is defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Casey enters the United States Naval Reserve and then the Office of Strategic Services, run from a converted campus of the National Institutes of Health on E Street. William Donovan's service is barely a year old and is improvising an American intelligence tradition out of lawyers, professors, bankers and burglars. Casey arrives as one of the lawyers. He will spend the rest of his life measuring institutions against this one, and when he is given the Central Intelligence Agency in nineteen eighty-one he takes it as a chance to build the OSS again.
suggested_refs: OSS headquarters at 2430 E Street NW, the old National Institutes of Health campus

stops.name: 70-72 Grosvenor Street, London, the invasion summer
stops.date_confidence: attested that OSS European operations ran from Grosvenor Street in 1944; Casey's rank and duties in June 1944 are reconstruction, and the correction matters, since he does not head Secret Intelligence until later that year
stops.campa: In the summer of the Normandy landings Casey is in London, a junior staff officer in David Bruce's OSS station in Mayfair. He is not yet running anything. The gathering pass placed the agent networks feeding order of battle toward the invasion beaches under his command, and the chronology runs the other way: the command comes to him months after the landings. He watches the largest intelligence effort of the war from inside it, at the desk level, and learns what it costs to put a man behind a line and get his report back out.
suggested_refs: OSS European Theater headquarters, 70-72 Grosvenor Street, Mayfair, under David Bruce

stops.name: Grosvenor Street, London, command of the Secret Intelligence Branch
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Wikipedia); the month of appointment is not fixed in the reachable sources, and December is chosen as late 1944, the period the pool gives
stops.campa: Late in nineteen forty-four Casey is made head of the OSS Secret Intelligence Branch for Europe. He is thirty-one, a lieutenant, and he now decides who goes into Germany. The Bronze Star follows. Four decades later, running an agency with a budget and a fleet, he will still describe this office as the real one, and will write a book to say so. The men he sends in are Germans, socialists, deserters and prisoners, and the operation is the closest thing to unmediated intelligence work he ever holds in his own hands.
suggested_refs: William J. Casey, The Secret War Against Hitler (1988), his own account of the SI command

stops.name: Berlin, the agents dropped into the collapsing Reich
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the operations are attested in Casey's own memoir but no specific drop sites were located, and Berlin stands here as a symbolic center of the target area rather than as a documented site
stops.campa: Under his direction OSS teams parachute agents into Germany to report troop movements and industrial targets ahead of the Allied advance. No drop site is named in anything reachable here, so Berlin holds the pin as the center of the country they fall into and not as a place Casey or his agents are recorded standing. He will call it the proudest work of his life. The source for that judgment is Casey himself, in a memoir published the year after he died, which is the least disinterested witness available and the only one this pass could reach.
suggested_refs: William J. Casey, The Secret War Against Hitler (1988); gap: specific drop sites not located
sources: William J. Casey, The Secret War Against Hitler (1988), via the research pool; gap: not read directly

stops.name: The United States Capitol, special counsel to a Senate committee
stops.date_confidence: span 1947-1948 attested (Wikipedia); month defaulted. The committee itself is not named in any reachable source, which is a gap
stops.campa: For two years after the war Casey serves as special counsel to a committee of the United States Senate. Which committee is not recorded in anything reachable here, and the gap is worth stating plainly, because it is the hinge between the war and the Washington career. He has been an intelligence officer and a tax editor; he now learns the third trade, which is the drafting of law in rooms where the arguing is done in advance. Forty years later he will be called back to this building to answer for Nicaragua.
suggested_refs: Senate committee records, 1947-1948; committee not identified in reachable sources

stops.name: Roslyn Harbor, the purchase of Locust Knoll
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Wikipedia); month and day not recorded and defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Casey buys eight and two-tenths acres at Roslyn Harbor with an eighteen fifty-four Jacobethan house on them, for fifty thousand dollars, and renames the place Mayknoll. It is his address for the remaining thirty-nine years of his life, through the SEC, the State Department, the campaign and the Agency. Wikipedia's infobox will later record Roslyn Harbor as the place he dies, and it is wrong: it is recording where he lived. The house is a residence, not a deathbed. He dies in a hospital eight miles up the shore.
suggested_refs: Mayknoll, formerly Locust Knoll, Roslyn Harbor, purchased 1948

stops.name: NYU School of Law, Washington Square, the tax lectures
stops.date_confidence: span 1948-1962 attested (Wikipedia); September chosen as the start of an academic year, not attested
stops.campa: The same year he buys the estate, Casey begins lecturing on tax law at New York University, and he keeps the lectureship for fourteen years while running a private practice and a publishing house at the same time. Two years into it he founds the Institute for Business Planning, another venture explaining the tax code to the people it binds. No address for the Institute was located, so it is recorded here rather than pinned. None of the three posts is given up for the other two, and the arrangement holds until nineteen sixty-two.
suggested_refs: NYU School of Law tax lectureship, 1948-1962; Institute for Business Planning, founded 1950

stops.name: Washington, the Point Four appointment and its impossible date
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and a flagged anachronism: Wikipedia dates his associate general counselship of the Point Four Program to 1948, but Point Four is named for the fourth point of Truman's inaugural address of 20 January 1949 and is not funded until the Act for International Development of 1950. The earliest possible date is 1949
stops.campa: Casey is recorded as associate general counsel to the Point Four Program, Truman's scheme for technical assistance to poor countries. The date attached to the claim cannot be right. Point Four takes its name from the fourth point of an inaugural address delivered in January nineteen forty-nine and is not funded until nineteen fifty, so no such program exists in the year the source assigns him to it. His federal legal work of nineteen forty-eight is more plausibly the Marshall Plan's Economic Cooperation Administration, but no document was found placing him there, and the guess is left as a guess.
suggested_refs: Britannica, 'Point Four Program'; Economic Cooperation Act, 3 April 1948
sources: Wikipedia, 'William J. Casey' (the source of the erroneous 1948)

stops.name: Manhattan, the long partnership at Hall, Casey, Dickler and Howley
stops.date_confidence: span 1957-1971 attested (Wikipedia); month defaulted. The coordinate is a generic Midtown point and not a located address, the same placeholder used for the Research Institute stop
stops.campa: For fourteen years Casey is a partner at Hall, Casey, Dickler and Howley, building the tax and corporate practice that makes his fortune and, more usefully, the Republican connections that make his career. The office address is not established in anything reachable, and the pin is a generic Midtown point carried for want of a better one. This is the platform. When Nixon reaches for a securities lawyer in nineteen seventy-one, and when Reagan reaches for a fundraiser in nineteen eighty, they are reaching into this firm's client list.
suggested_refs: Hall, Casey, Dickler and Howley, New York, 1957-1971; office address not located

stops.name: Nassau County, the primary he loses
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Wikipedia); month not recorded and defaulted within the primary season. The coordinate is a central-Nassau point standing for the district, not a located site
stops.campa: Casey runs for the Republican nomination in New York's third congressional district and is beaten in the primary by a former congressman, Steven Derounian. He never reaches a general election. The research pool contradicted itself on this point, calling him the party's candidate in one lens and a primary loser in another, and the wikitext settles it: defeated in the primary. It is the only time he asks anyone to vote for him. Every office he holds afterward, and there are five, is given to him by a president.
suggested_refs: Republican primary, New York's 3rd congressional district, 1966
sources: Wikipedia, 'William J. Casey' (wikitext: 'defeated in the primary by former Congressman Steven Derounian')

stops.name: 500 North Capitol Street NW, chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (Wikipedia). Coordinate corrected: the pool's 38.8974, -77.0138 matches no SEC headquarters, and the Commission sat at 500 North Capitol Street NW until 1988
stops.campa: Nixon makes Casey chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission on the fourteenth of April, nineteen seventy-one, and he serves twenty-two months, through the reorganization that follows Wall Street's back-office collapse. The tax lawyer now writes the rules he spent thirty years reading. The coordinate here required repair: the research pool pinned the Commission in the wrong blocks entirely, and in these years the SEC sits at 500 North Capitol Street, four blocks from the Senate committee room he had served as counsel a generation earlier.
suggested_refs: SEC headquarters, 500 North Capitol Street NW, occupied until the 1988 move to 450 Fifth Street NW

stops.name: 2201 C Street NW, Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian). The department's modern listing renders the title as Under Secretary for Economic Growth, Energy, and the Environment; the discrepancy is recorded and not resolved
stops.campa: On the second of February, nineteen seventy-three, Casey moves from the SEC to the State Department as Under Secretary for Economic Affairs, and for thirteen months he runs American foreign economic policy: trade, aid, the arrangements between governments about money. It is the overt version of a relationship he will conduct covertly a decade later from Langley, with several of the same countries. The Office of the Historian fixes both his dates. It also gives the post a different name now, a small reminder that even official titles shift with time.
suggested_refs: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian, principal officers listing
sources: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian, history.state.gov

stops.name: 811 Vermont Avenue NW, chairman of the Export-Import Bank
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (Wikipedia); tenure ends 2 January 1976. The concurrent service on the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board, 1975-1976, is attested but has no separate located address
stops.campa: Casey chairs the Export-Import Bank of the United States for twenty-two months, financing American trade abroad, and in his last year there Ford also seats him on the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board. He now sits at two desks: the overseas movement of money on one, the oversight of secret services on the other. He learns at Vermont Avenue which banks in which countries will move a payment without asking what it is for, and the knowledge does not leave him when he goes.
suggested_refs: Export-Import Bank of the United States, 811 Vermont Avenue NW

stops.name: Manhattan, of counsel at Rogers and Wells
stops.date_confidence: span 1976-1981 attested (Wikipedia); month defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Out of government under Carter, Casey returns to private practice as of counsel to Rogers and Wells, and among his clients are the governments of Indonesia and South Korea. He is sixty-three, rich, and represents foreign states for a living in the interval between running an American bank and running American intelligence. The five years are the only ones since nineteen forty-three in which he holds no federal office at all, and he spends them acquiring precisely the kind of client relationships that a director of central intelligence is not supposed to have.
suggested_refs: Rogers and Wells, New York; Casey's Indonesian and South Korean government representations

stops.name: Manhattan, the founding of ICEPS with Antony Fisher
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Wikipedia); month defaulted. The coordinate is an unsourced placeholder sitting about sixty metres from the Rogers and Wells pin, not a founding address
stops.campa: Casey and the British economist Antony Fisher found a free-market policy institute in New York. Its name in nineteen seventy-eight is the International Center for Economic Policy Studies; it becomes the Manhattan Institute for Policy Research only in nineteen eighty-one, and calling it that in the founding year would be an anachronism this account avoids. The institute outlives him by decades and shapes American urban policy. He is by then a co-founder in name, having left New York for Langley three years after the signing.
suggested_refs: International Center for Economic Policy Studies, founded 1978, renamed Manhattan Institute for Policy Research 1981

stops.name: 901 South Highland Street, Arlington, taking over the campaign
stops.date_confidence: attested that Casey took over in early 1980 after John Sears was dismissed; the day is not fixed here and February is a placeholder. Coordinate corrected from the pool's 38.8929, -77.0888, which lands in Rosslyn about 3.3 km away
stops.campa: John Sears is dismissed and Casey takes the management of Ronald Reagan's presidential campaign, running it from a headquarters on South Highland Street in Arlington. He is sixty-six, has never managed a campaign, and wins. The pool attached a further claim, that he helped broker the alliance that put George Bush on the ticket, and the cited article does not contain it; the Detroit decision is usually laid to the collapse of the Ford talks instead. The clause is dropped rather than repeated. What is attested is enough: he delivers the presidency and names his own price.
suggested_refs: Reagan for President headquarters, 901 South Highland Street, Arlington, Virginia

stops.name: Arlington, the Carter briefing papers
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the episode later called Debategate is attested but the exact timing and Casey's role are disputed among sources, and the date is the pool's pin rather than a fixed one
stops.campa: Classified Carter administration briefing papers for the presidential debate reach the Reagan campaign. The episode acquires a name, Debategate, only three years later, when a congressional inquiry works over who passed what to whom. Casey is asked and does not remember. Whether the papers arrive before the debate of the twenty-eighth of October or after it, and whether they pass through his hands at all, the sources do not agree, and nothing here settles it. The pin marks the campaign office, which is the one place everyone agrees the papers ended up.
suggested_refs: The 1983 congressional inquiry into the Carter debate briefing papers
sources: Wikipedia, 'William J. Casey' (noting the dispute over timing and attribution)

stops.name: Madrid, the meeting that is said to have happened
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and contested: the Iranian intermediary Jamshid Hashemi alleged meetings at the Hotel Ritz in July and August 1980, and the House task force reported on 13 January 1993 that these allegations are fabrications
stops.campa: The legend says Casey comes to Madrid in the summer before the election and meets Mehdi and Hassan Karroubi at the Hotel Ritz to arrange that the American hostages in Tehran stay hostages until after the voting. The legend has a single named source, the Iranian intermediary Jamshid Hashemi. Newsweek accounts for Casey's movements in that window and puts him at a conference in London. The House task force reports in January nineteen ninety-three that the Madrid allegations are fabrications. The story is repeated anyway, and goes on being repeated.
suggested_refs: Report of the House October Surprise Task Force, 13 January 1993; Newsweek, November 1991

stops.name: Central Intelligence Agency headquarters, Langley, sworn in with Cabinet rank
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (Wikipedia); tenure ends 29 January 1987
stops.campa: On the twenty-eighth of January, nineteen eighty-one, Casey is sworn in as Director of Central Intelligence and given Cabinet rank, which no director has held before. He is sixty-seven and has waited thirty-five years to have Donovan's job. From Langley he rebuilds the covert action capacity that the Church Committee reforms stripped out in the seventies and turns it toward anti-communist insurgencies from Afghanistan to Nicaragua. Stansfield Turner, who hands him the building, will title his own chapter on these years The Resurrection of "Wild Bill".
stops.quote_source: Stansfield Turner, Burn Before Reading: Presidents, CIA Directors, and Secret Intelligence (Hyperion, 2005), chapter nine subtitle, verified from the book's own table of contents and chapter head. Not a sentence Turner spoke in 1981.
suggested_refs: The Original Headquarters Building at Langley; Stansfield Turner, Burn Before Reading (2005), chapter nine
sources: Stansfield Turner, Burn Before Reading (2005), extracted directly

stops.name: Tegucigalpa, the station behind the Contra camps
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; Honduras as the base of Contra operations through 1981-1986 is general Contra-war geography and is not itemized to Casey by name in the reachable source
stops.campa: Honduras holds the main Contra base camps and a large CIA station supporting the war against the Sandinistas, the war Casey presses Reagan to fund and Congress repeatedly moves to defund through the Boland amendments. He is the advocate in the Cabinet Room and the paymaster at Langley. The Honduran ground itself is not itemized to him in anything reachable here, and the pin marks the theater rather than a visit. Manuel Noriega is running Panamanian intelligence at the far end of the same isthmus, on a payroll the Agency opened in nineteen seventy-one.
suggested_refs: The Boland Amendments; CIA station Tegucigalpa, 1981-1986

stops.name: The Apostolic Palace, Vatican City, the reported Roman briefings
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the account rests on Bob Woodward's Veil alone, with no itemized dates, and the year is a placeholder inside the reported 1981-1986 period. Coordinate corrected from the pool's 41.9029, 12.4534, which is St. Peter's Basilica
stops.campa: Woodward reports that Casey flies secretly to Rome in a windowless C-141 and is taken undercover to the Vatican to brief John Paul II on the Soviet bloc during the Polish crisis. There are no dates, no manifests and no second witness; the whole of it stands on one journalist's book. This project tags the same journalist's deathbed account as reconstruction, and consistency requires the same tag here. The Fordham graduate briefing a pope on Poland is too good a sentence to promote without evidence. It is entered as what it is, a report.
suggested_refs: Bob Woodward, Veil: The Secret Wars of the CIA 1981-1987 (1987), the sole source for the Vatican flights
sources: Wikipedia, 'William J. Casey' (citing Woodward); gap: individual visit dates not specified

stops.name: The White House Situation Room, backing the arms channel to Iran
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month (Wikipedia, 'Iran-Contra affair'); day defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Robert McFarlane drafts a directive proposing arms sales to Iran as a channel of influence in Tehran and a route to the Americans held hostage in Lebanon. Inside the National Security Planning Group the proposal is argued and mostly opposed. The reachable summary is blunt about who is on which side, and it is a paraphrase rather than his own words, so it is quoted as a paraphrase. Casey is the director of central intelligence supporting a policy his own analysts think will not work, which is the position he occupies for the next eighteen months.
stops.quote: Only the director of the CIA William J. Casey supported McFarlane's plan to start selling arms to Iran.
stops.quote_source: Wikipedia, 'Iran-Contra affair', section 'Arms sales to Iran'. A third-party paraphrase of Casey's position, not a Casey utterance.
suggested_refs: The June 1985 McFarlane draft national security decision directive on Iran

stops.name: Ilopango Air Base, El Salvador, the resupply field
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; Casey's direct operational knowledge of Ilopango specifically is disputed and is not confirmed by the reachable source. Coordinate inherited byte-identically from manuel_noriega.journey.json rather than from this pool's own figure
stops.campa: Contra resupply flights stage out of Ilopango, carrying arms and stores north into Nicaragua through a network Oliver North runs from the National Security Council staff. Manuel Noriega's own record states plainly that North and Casey run the operation from the other end. Whether Casey knows this particular runway by name is disputed and unproven. The two men never meet on paper, but the same covert network runs through both of their hands.
suggested_refs: Ilopango Air Base as the Contra resupply hub, 1985-1986

stops.name: Panama City, the asset inherited
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; no primary Casey-Noriega record was located in the sources consulted, and the relationship is documented at the institutional level only
stops.campa: Manuel Noriega keeps an intelligence relationship with the Agency throughout Casey's directorship, later picked apart amid the Contra-supply and drug-trafficking inquiries of the period. Casey did not open the file. Noriega has been on the payroll since nineteen seventy-one and his status was renewed in nineteen seventy-six by George Bush, who is now the vice president in the room. What Casey inherits is a Panamanian officer already paid for and already the kind of asset a later administration will invade a country to arrest.
suggested_refs: Senate Kerry Committee inquiry into Contra supply and narcotics
sources: manuel_noriega.journey.json (1971 payroll; 1976 continuation approved by Bush)
General Iran-Contra era reporting; gap: no primary Casey-Noriega record located

stops.name: Tehran, the cake and the missile parts
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month for McFarlane's trip (Wikipedia, 'Iran-Contra affair'); Casey's own presence in Tehran is not documented anywhere reachable and is not claimed
stops.campa: McFarlane flies into Tehran in May nineteen eighty-six carrying a planeload of missile parts and a cake, on the initiative Casey has backed in Washington since the previous June. Nothing is settled. The hostages are not released on the terms discussed and the channel begins to leak within months. Casey is not on the aircraft; no source places him in Iran at any point, and the pin marks the destination of a policy he sponsored rather than a journey he made. Thirty-seven years earlier the Shah had come to Washington to ask for American arms, and got them openly.
suggested_refs: McFarlane's May 1986 Tehran mission
sources: Wikipedia, 'Iran-Contra affair'; gap: no record of Casey traveling to Iran

stops.name: Leadenhall Street, London, inside the diagram
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to Casey; the BCCI principal office and the Kerry Committee findings are attested, but Casey's placement inside the network is an assertion carried by this atlas's own files rather than by an external document
stops.campa: The Bank of Credit and Commerce International keeps its principal office in the City, and the Senate report on it will find ties to intelligence services, to arms dealing and to Noriega. Agha Hasan Abedi's bank and Manuel Noriega's accounts sit inside the same web: the artist Mark Lombardi will later draw this network as arcs and nodes, with Abedi and Clark Clifford and North and Casey inside it. It is a connection asserted rather than proved by any single document. Saddam Hussein reaches the same grey channels from the other direction, a decade on.
suggested_refs: Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee (Kerry Committee) report on BCCI; Mark Lombardi's BCCI-Iran-Contra drawings

stops.name: The United States Capitol, the testimony he does give
stops.date_confidence: attested that Casey appeared before the Senate and House intelligence committees in November and again in December 1986 (Walsh, Final Report); the exact day in November is not fixed here and the pin date is approximate
stops.campa: The arms sales to Iran and the diversion of their proceeds to the Contras become public in November nineteen eighty-six, and Casey goes up to the intelligence committees to answer for them. He testifies in November and again in December. This matters because the received version says his illness stopped him from ever testifying, and it did not: he had already been in the room. Walsh's report records the December appearance in a single flat clause. What the illness stops is everything after the fifteenth, which is where the story of his silence actually begins.
suggested_refs: Casey's November and December 1986 appearances before the Senate and House intelligence committees; transcripts not retrieved
sources: Lawrence E. Walsh, Final Report of the Independent Counsel for Iran/Contra Matters (1993)

stops.name: Georgetown University Hospital, the seizures
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (Wikipedia). Coordinate corrected from the pool's 38.9075, -77.0723, which lands about 490 m off campus; the hospital at 3800 Reservoir Road NW is at 38.9112, -77.0753
stops.campa: On the fifteenth of December Casey suffers seizures in his office and is taken to Georgetown University Hospital. He is seventy-three. Three days later surgeons open his skull and find a lymphoma nobody had diagnosed, sitting in the brain of the man who has been the government's chief keeper of secrets for six years. He never returns to Langley. The timing has fed suspicion ever since. The medical record, so far as it is reachable, gives a tumor that had been growing a long while in a man who did not know he was ill.
suggested_refs: MedStar Georgetown University Hospital, 3800 Reservoir Road NW

stops.name: The United States Capitol, the hearing of the sixteenth of December
stops.date_confidence: attested as scheduled (Wikipedia); the appearance does not take place
stops.campa: Casey is due before Congress on the sixteenth of December to be asked what he knew about the diversion. The chair is empty. He had answered questions in that building a few weeks before and would have answered more, and instead the record stops at the edge of the only session anyone afterward wanted the transcript of. One contradiction is left standing here rather than smoothed: a separate account describes him as hospitalized for a stroke rather than a tumor. Both readings are in the sources. Neither is preferred here.
suggested_refs: The cancelled 16 December 1986 congressional appearance

stops.name: Georgetown University Hospital, the nod Woodward reports
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; Woodward dates the visit to January 1987 and the account is adamantly denied by Casey's widow. UPI and the Los Angeles Times independently place the claimed visit at Georgetown University Hospital, not at a Manhattan or Bethesda hospital as the research pool variously had it
stops.campa: Bob Woodward writes that he got into the room for four minutes, asked the dying man whether he had known about the diversion of the Iran money to the Contras, and got an answer without words. The family says he was never there. Colleagues say the same. The book comes out the year Casey dies and the scene is the most quoted thing about him, which is a peculiar fate for a man who spent forty years arranging for things not to be quoted. Walsh will find no document supporting what the nod is said to have meant.
stops.quote: His head jerked up hard. He stared, and finally nodded yes.
stops.quote_source: Bob Woodward, Veil: The Secret Wars of the CIA 1981-1987 (Simon and Schuster, 1987). Woodward's own narration of the reported bedside exchange, not Casey's speech; denied by Sofia Casey.
suggested_refs: Bob Woodward, Veil (1987), the hospital-room passage

stops.name: Georgetown University Hospital, the resignation
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (Wikipedia); he has been formally on leave since 18 December 1986
stops.campa: On the twenty-ninth of January, nineteen eighty-seven, Casey's tenure as Director of Central Intelligence ends. He has been formally on leave since the surgery six weeks earlier and has not set foot in the building since the seizures. Six years and one day after taking the oath with Cabinet rank he leaves the post by letter, from a hospital, with the largest questions about his conduct unanswered and unanswerable. The Agency he wanted since nineteen forty-five, and got, he holds for exactly as long as his brain permits.
suggested_refs: Casey's resignation as Director of Central Intelligence, 29 January 1987

segments.name: Glen Cove and the Long Afterlife

stops.name: Glen Cove Hospital, Long Island, death of pneumonia
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. Place corrected: the New York Times, UPI and the Sun-Sentinel all place the death in a hospital at Glen Cove; Wikipedia's infobox 'Roslyn Harbor' records his residence, not his place of death
stops.campa: Casey dies of pneumonia on the sixth of May, nineteen eighty-seven, aged seventy-four, in a hospital at Glen Cove, eight miles up the shore from the house he bought in nineteen forty-eight. The obituaries agree on the ground: Glen Cove Community Hospital, not Mayknoll. The encyclopaedia that carries most of the rest of his dates puts Roslyn Harbor in the box, because Roslyn Harbor is where he lived, and the two facts have been folded into one ever since. He dies four months after the last question was put to him and never answered.
suggested_refs: Glen Cove Hospital, 101 St Andrews Lane; New York Times obituary, 7 May 1987

stops.name: Church of Saint Mary, Roslyn, the bishop at the pulpit
stops.date_confidence: month attested (Wikipedia); the exact day of the Requiem Mass is not fixed in the reachable sources. Coordinate standardized to OSM, 100 Bryant Avenue, against three different figures carried in the research pool
stops.campa: The Requiem Mass is said by Fr. Daniel Fagan at St. Mary's in Roslyn, a mile and a half from the estate. Bishop John R. McGann presides, and from the pulpit, with the President and Mrs. Reagan in the pews, he criticizes the dead man's ethics and what he did in Nicaragua. It is the only judgment delivered on Casey in his own hearing, so to speak, and it is delivered by his own Church at his own funeral. The Jesuits taught him to argue. The diocese buries him with an argument.

stops.name: Cemetery of the Holy Rood, Westbury, the grave
stops.date_confidence: month attested (Wikipedia); day not fixed. Coordinate standardized to OSM against two conflicting figures in the research pool
stops.campa: He is buried at the Cemetery of the Holy Rood in Westbury, closing a circuit of about twenty miles. Bellmore to Roslyn Harbor to Glen Cove to Westbury: a childhood, an estate, a deathbed and a grave, all inside one county of Long Island, wrapped around a working life spent in London, Washington, Rome and Central America. His widow Sophia, whom the sources also call Sofia and who spent the last of his years denying that a reporter ever got into his room, is buried in the year two thousand.

stops.name: The New Headquarters Building, Langley, the plaque
stops.date_confidence: undated in the reachable sources beyond 'after 1987'; 1991 is the completion of the annex and is a placeholder. Coordinate corrected: the pool pinned the Original Headquarters Building, and Wikipedia places the plaque in the New Headquarters Building lobby
stops.campa: A commemorative plaque to Casey goes up in the lobby of the New Headquarters Building at Langley, the annex rather than the original block, and nobody records the date. The Agency he rebuilt keeps him on its wall. In the same decade Joseph Persico publishes the biography that becomes the standard secondary account of his life, and Steve Coll folds his Afghan and Nicaraguan programs into Ghost Wars, so that the covert war he ran turns into a chapter in books sold in airports. The plaque and the paperbacks are the same act of preservation.
suggested_refs: The CIA New Headquarters Building lobby plaque; Joseph E. Persico, Casey (1991); Steve Coll, Ghost Wars (2004)

stops.name: Paris, the deal alleged four years after his death
stops.date_confidence: the op-ed is attested to April 1991; the allegation it makes is reconstruction and is not corroborated. Day defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Gary Sick publishes an opinion piece in the New York Times alleging that Casey and other Reagan campaign officials made a secret deal with Iran in Paris in October nineteen eighty to hold the hostages past the election. Casey has been dead four years and cannot be asked. The charge produces a congressional task force, which reports in nineteen ninety-three that the linked Madrid allegations are fabrications. Nothing about Paris is proven and nothing is disproven either, which is the condition in which the accusation has stayed ever since.
suggested_refs: Gary Sick, New York Times op-ed, April 1991

stops.name: Washington, the Independent Counsel's finding
stops.date_confidence: the Final Report is attested to 1993; the research pool does not fix the month, so day and month are defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Lawrence Walsh closes the Iran-Contra investigation with a finding stated in one sentence: Independent Counsel obtained no documentary evidence showing Casey knew about or approved the diversion. The same report says his conduct in the autumn of nineteen eighty-six was more consistent with the behavior of a person aware of it. Both halves stand. The only direct testimony tying him to early knowledge came from Oliver North, uncorroborated, and Casey denied it while he could still speak. This is the closest thing to a verdict the record contains.
stops.quote: Independent Counsel obtained no documentary evidence showing Casey knew about or approved the diversion.
stops.quote_source: Lawrence E. Walsh, Final Report of the Independent Counsel for Iran/Contra Matters (1993), chapter 15.

stops.name: Hoover Institution Archives, Stanford, the papers
stops.date_confidence: undated; no date of deposit is established in any reachable source, and the pin is placed at the end of the sequence rather than at an attested moment
stops.campa: Casey's personal and official papers come to rest at the Hoover Institution on the Stanford campus, three thousand miles from Bellmore, and become the archival basis for whatever is written about him next. No finding aid was retrieved in this pass and the year of deposit is not established. The record ends in boxes catalogued by people who never met him, waiting for a reader patient enough to check what Wikipedia has been repeating about a man born in a city it cannot name the neighborhood of.
suggested_refs: Hoover Institution Archives, William J. Casey papers; finding aid not retrieved
